subject: Neuroscience
textbook: Neuroscience: Exploring the Brain, 3e (Bear et al.)
title: Receptive field
prompt:
Create a 28-second silent English 1920×1080 educational animation about Receptive field for Introduction to Neuroscience.
Use Remotion 4.0.410, React 19 and the introduction-to-neuroscience course kit. Reproduce the actual video in assets/source-kits/introduction-to-neuroscience/src/videos/ns08-receptive-field.tsx; fps is 30.
Keep the same dark course palette and diagrams. Use the actual state transitions from the source, not a generic neural-network animation.

Scene plan:
1. 0–5s, baseline: Steady illustrative baseline spike train advances at 20 Hz Why: Retinal ganglion cells can fire spontaneously Visible result: Baseline provides the comparison for every subsequent probe
2. 5–12s, center: Spot appears at dx=0; firing rises from baseline to 80 Hz and spike spacing narrows Why: Light in the ON-center increases this cell’s response Visible result: Position and measured rate change together
3. 12–20s, surround: Probe switches location with an intervening baseline; response falls to 0 Hz and spikes pause Why: Surround illumination antagonizes the center response Visible result: Less firing despite the same spot brightness
4. 20–28s, outside: Rate returns to 20 Hz; spikes resume at baseline; center and surround markers retain opposing signs Why: The outside probe does not stimulate the modeled receptive field Visible result: Spatial tests define where this neuron’s activity is changed

All on-screen labels and narration-equivalent captions are concise English. Use no spoken audio or music. Preserve the specific objects, state bindings and timing above. Render the registered composition for this slug and inspect the final MP4 at the stored risk moments.
Reproduction requires the packaged TSX source, the course kit, Remotion/React dependencies, Chromium and ffmpeg. This prompt describes the reviewed artifact; it is not a self-contained promise of pixel-identical reproduction without those files.
final_title: Receptive Field: Center and Surround Responses
learning_objective: Predict how a small light spot in an ON-center retinal ganglion cell receptive field changes firing relative to baseline.
core_conclusion: A receptive field is the stimulus region that changes a neuron’s activity; center and surround can act oppositely.

references.title: Visual Responses of Ganglion Cells
references.supports: ON-center receptive fields, antagonistic surround and spot mapping

requirement_prompt:
Create a 15-second silent educational animation in Manim Community Edition.

Explain “Receptive field” using this visual metaphor: “a glowing neural circuit carrying one signal for Receptive field”. Dynamically demonstrate the core formula or conclusion: A receptive field is the stimulus region that changes one neuron's activity..

Use one continuous scene and one clear narrative line. Explain only this concept; do not add comparisons, extensions, or side cases. Structure the motion in three connected beats:
1. 0–3 seconds: establish the objects, input, or initial state.
2. 3–10.95 seconds: show at least two causally connected state changes that reveal the mechanism and progressively connect key variables or conclusions to the visual.
3. 10.95–12.45 seconds: resolve the result, invariant, or central insight.

Keep introducing meaningful animation information until 12.45 seconds. Hold the final still frame for no more than 2.55 seconds.

All on-screen titles, labels, and supporting annotations must be short English phrases in Arial. Use a bright, non-black background (#F4EEF8); main visual (#214E75); secondary visual (#8A2356); highlight (#725400); and text (#172033). Maintain strong contrast and legibility.

Strict typography requirements:
- Render every complete title, label, phrase, or sentence as one native Text(...) object so every character shares one baseline.
- Never rebuild a line from separately positioned word or letter objects, and never align words by their individual bounding boxes.
- Create Arial text at a base font_size of 64, then uniformly scale the complete Text object to its final visual size; do not render explanatory text directly at a tiny font size.
- Preserve ordinary spaces inside the same Text object, set disable_ligatures=True, and do not add manual tracking, special-width spaces, or per-character offsets.

Use ThreeDScene for a genuinely spatial main visual: at least one core object must show volume, depth, or occlusion, and include one smooth camera move that reveals spatial structure. The 3D motion must clarify the concept rather than merely tilt a flat diagram. Render in 16:9.

Global rendering requirements:
- Never place plain English words, sentences, titles, or explanatory prose in MathTex, Tex, or inline LaTeX math mode. Use the native Text(...) component for all explanatory text and titles.
- If an English word is unavoidable inside a mathematical expression, explicitly wrap every word with \text{...}; never leave a word bare in algebra mode.
- Animate text at whole-word or whole-line granularity. Never split text into individually spaced letters or animate isolated letter spans.
- Do not use text-align: justify or the SVG textLength or lengthAdjust attributes.
- Use the final conclusion display as the video's opening poster frame; do not begin on an empty background.

production.scene_rationale: Four scenes establish one cell and baseline, test its center, test its surround, and test an outside location. Each probe changes a spatial cause while preserving the same recorded neuron; removing any test loses the opposing sign or field boundary.

critical_processes.uncertainty: Spot geometry must stay completely inside each sampled region and rates must drive spikes as well as labels.
critical_processes.expected_observation: Center spot gives dense spikes; surround spot suppresses them; outside restores baseline.

bindings.spot: ReceptiveField spot and SVG probe position
bindings.rate: ReceptiveField bar/label plus actual scrolling spike population derived from rate

assertions: No probe and outside spot produce 20 Hz.
Center gives 80 Hz; surround gives 0 Hz, never negative.
Probe radius 12 fits wholly in radius-72 center or annulus 72..160; no area-integration claim.
